title: The Wreck of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Edmund Voss, a disgraced mountain guide working the windswept Atlantic coast of Patagonia, is hired by a wealthy Argentine family to lead an expedition to a sea cave exposed only at extreme low tide — a cave their patriarch's journals claim holds the remains of a 1912 shipwreck and the gold that vanished with it. Inside, Voss discovers not treasure but evidence: ledgers proving the family fortune was built on betrayed shipwreck survivors left to die, including her own grandfather. As the dry season drains the coast and the family moves to silence her, Voss must choose between the justice of exposure and the survival of her team, ultimately smuggling the ledgers out and burning the cave's entrance behind them, letting the sea keep its secret while the truth reaches the newspapers.
about_author: Quentin Underhill is the pen name of a former merchant marine officer who spent a decade running supply routes along the Patagonian coast before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels from a farmhouse in Chubut Province, where he keeps a collection of salvaged ship's logs.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Books
chapters.summary: Voss, blacklisted and broke in Puerto Deseado, takes a lucrative contract from matriarch Inés Aldao to guide an expedition to a cave visible only at record low tides. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: wary pride — she needs this job more than she trusts the people offering it.

chapters.title: A Family of Anchors
chapters.summary: At the Aldao estancia, Voss meets the expedition team: Inés's brittle grandson Tomás, marine archaeologist Camila Reyes, and fixer Bruno Sartori whose loyalty is clearly for sale. The patriarch's 1912 journals are shown under supervision. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: unease dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: The first descent into the cave at spring low tide reveals a wrecked longboat, human bones arranged with care, and a sealed iron chest. Tomás panics as the tide turns; Voss gets everyone out but must leave the chest. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Chest Said
chapters.summary: Camila secretly photographs documents from the chest: shipwreck survivor lists marked 'expended' in the Aldao patriarch's hand. She shows Voss, who recognizes her grandfather's name among the abandoned. POV: alternating Voss and Camila. Emotional beat: grief igniting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Inés offers Voss a fortune to declare the cave empty of interest; Bruno quietly warns what happens to guides who refuse. Voss realizes the expedition was never about discovery but containment. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: cold clarity — she has been hired to bury her own history.

chapters.title: Bruno's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sartori defects, revealing three generations of Aldao 'fixers' who made problems disappear, including Voss's father, ruined after asking questions in the 1980s. The team fractures: Tomás wants it buried, Camila wants it published. POV: Sartori. Emotional beat: a mercenary's guilt finally finding a price he won't take.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: With the tides failing, the window to recover the original ledgers closes. Inés cuts the expedition short and seals the estancia; radio contact with town goes suspiciously dead. Voss plans a night run back to the cave against the calendar. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: cornered resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Ebb
chapters.summary: Voss, Camila, and Bruno cross forty miles of salt flats by night to reach the cave on the season's final extreme low tide, pursued by Tomás and hired men. They retrieve the originals as the water rises faster than forecast. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce competence.

chapters.title: What the Sea Was Owed
chapters.summary: Trapped by the returning tide inside the cave mouth, Voss confronts Tomás, who has followed them down; she offers him the choice his family never gave the castaways. He stands aside. They escape through a blowhole passage as the cave floods. POV: alternating Voss and Tomás. Emotional beat: mercy as the harder justice.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the ledgers reach a Buenos Aires paper; investigations begin, Inés dies before testifying, and the estancia passes to Tomás, who funds a memorial for the 1912 dead. Voss walks the coast at high tide, name still blacklisted, conscience clear. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: quiet, unglamorous peace.
